callerDataMutation.text: This writes into data the caller passed in. The change reaches the caller, and nothing at the call site says it will: the call reads like it hands data over, and the caller's data comes back different. Return what changed and let the caller write it, or build a new value from the parameter.

processStateWithoutReason.text: This `@processState` tag gives no reason. The tag exempts every write through a parameter of this type from nexus/correctness-no-caller-data-mutation, so it has to say why the type is state the process shares rather than data a caller hands over: `@processState <why>`. Until it does, it exempts nothing.

mutatesWithoutReason.text: This [[tag]] names its parameter but gives no reason. [[exempts]] from [[rule]], so it has to say why the parameter is an out-parameter by contract: [[form]]. Until it does, it exempts nothing.

exempts.TypeScript: The tag exempts every write through that parameter, in this method and in every method that overrides or implements it,
exempts.Go: The comment exempts every write through that parameter in this function

mutatesUnknownParameter.text: This [[tag]] names no parameter of its [[function]]. It reads [[form]], and the first word has to be one of this [[function]]'s parameter names, so as written it exempts nothing. A [[tagWord]] left behind by a rename is the usual cause.
